printed_convention: AFND cytokine locus label IL-6/ - 174: a promoter offset in bp upstream of the IL6 transcription start site, alleles quoted on the gene sense strand
strand_evidence: G/C is palindromic, so the round-trip has no power here. Strand comes from the co-named non-palindromic locus in the same scheme: pmid:10747905 (Terry 2000, J Biol Chem 275:18138-44) names -597G-->A, -572G-->C and -174G-->C as one IL6 promoter haplotype scheme; LitVar2 maps -597G>A to rs1800797, and Ensembl release 116 Variant Recoder and dbSNP build 157 both place rs1800797 at NC_000007.14:22726601:A:G, so the plus-strand reference there is A (rs1800797 is itself multi-allelic on GRCh38 per dbSNP build 157 - A:C, A:G, A:T - but this argument needs only that the plus-strand reference allele is A, which holds regardless of which alternate is considered). A minus-strand reading of that scheme would print C/T at -597 and would not contain the reference allele at all, so the scheme prints plus-strand letters and the -174 G/C printed here are plus-strand. Ensembl 116 independently annotates IL6 (ENSG00000136244) on strand +1 and VEP reports rs1800795 as an upstream_gene_variant at distance 174 from the canonical transcript ENST00000258743. A second check settles the orientation without leaning on the naming convention at all: under a minus-strand reading the allele the internal id calls minor (the -c suffix, assigned by MINOR_ALLELE_RULE in genomeos/observations/sources/afnd_cytokines.py) would map to plus-strand G, whose global frequency dbSNP build 157 reports as 0.750 in TOPMED and 0.859 in 1000Genomes; this repository's own published AFND observations for cyt:il-6-174-c give a median of 0.304 across 83 populations, with 1 of 83 above 0.6. A minus reading is irreconcilable with both, so plus is the only consistent orientation. Design §6 rejects frequency concordance as the step-1 method because it has no power near 0.5; here the two hypotheses sit at 0.30 against 0.75-0.86, so the comparison does discriminate, and it is used as corroboration of strand rather than to choose the rsID.
reference_resource: Ensembl release 116 Variant Recoder, GRCh38, and NCBI dbSNP build 157 RefSNP API; both independently return NC_000007.14:22727025:C:G
naming_citation: pmid:25526459 states SNP in the IL-6 gene rs1800795 (-174 G/C); corroborated by pmid:37904417 which states IL-6 gene -174G/C locus (rs1800795); both sit in the LitVar2 trail for rs1800795
notes: rs1800795 is multi-allelic on GRCh38 (C>G and C>T); the C>G allele is the one the printed G/C pair selects. GRCh38 carries C here, so the literature wild-type G is not the reference allele - the same pattern holds at IL-6 -597, which is what makes the strand argument self-consistent. VEP distance 174 matches the legacy offset exactly, but the neighbouring -597 locus sits at VEP distance 598, so the legacy numbering is not internally consistent to the base and the offset alone was not treated as proof of naming.
